title: Some AI browsers come with major security risks
author: U. Washington
excerpt: A University of Washington study finds that agentic browsers can create cybersecurity risks through prompt injection, memory poisoning and weakened same-origin protections.

title: AI tools are surprisingly vulnerable to targeted attacks
author: Matt Shipman-NC State
excerpt: Research shows that adversarial attacks can manipulate data fed into artificial intelligence tools and force systems to make bad decisions, a foundational security concern for tool-using agents.

title: AI-generated code is vulnerable
author: Georgia Tech
excerpt: Researchers find recurring security weaknesses in code produced with generative AI tools, a practical risk for coding agents and AI-assisted software workflows.

title: Social media policies are no match for AI bots
author: Brandi Wampler-Notre Dame
excerpt: Research finds that social media platforms are not doing enough to stop harmful AI bots, a foundational case for studying autonomous accounts and platform safety.

title: How flocking birds can help make AI better
author: James Devitt-NYU
excerpt: New research draws from flocking bird patterns to help AI produce more reliable outputs, connecting collective intelligence with multi-agent coordination.

title: Simple tweak could cut AI chatbots' reinforcement of false beliefs
author: Georgia Tech
excerpt: Research examines how agreeable AI chatbots can reinforce false beliefs, a useful safety case for assistants that interact with people.
